messages.subject: Re: question about methylkit input files
parts:
Hi Haiyan,

To extract data from the diffAnn object you can use two functions ‘getAssociationWithTSS(diffAnn)’ and 'getMembers(diffAnn)’. The first function will give you per site the distance to nearest gene and and the NCBI gene ID, while the second returns the genomic feature assignment of the site. Both functions return data.frames with the same number of rows as your myDiff25p object, so you could ‘cbind’ those data.frames and save all to a csv file.

Best,
Alex



> On 27. May 2021, at 21:08, Lei, Haiyan (NIH/NCI) [C] <lei.h...@nih.gov> wrote:
>
> Hi, Alex:
>
> Thanks for the suggestion. It worked. Sorry I have one more question, how I can get the annotation table for the diffAnn, such as the myDiff25p.csv file did not corresponding to the gene name; From the tutorial, I didn’t find how to save the annotated diffAnn to the csv file. Thanks.
>
> > diffAnn=annotateWithGeneParts(as(myDiff25p,"GRanges"),gene.obj)
> > write.table(diffAnn,"diffAnn.csv", sep=",",row.names = F)
> Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE) :
> cannot coerce class ‘structure("AnnotationByGeneParts", package = "genomation")’ to a data.frame
>
>
> best
>
> Haiyan
> From: Alexander Blume <alex....@gmail.com>
> Sent: Thursday, May 27, 2021 2:30 PM
> To: Lei, Haiyan (NIH/NCI) [C] <lei.h...@nih.gov>
> Subject: Re: question about methylkit input files
>
> Hi Haiyan,
>
>
> I am happy it worked so far.
>
> To answer your first question, you have two options to save the output of the bam processing. Either you use the 'save.context' argument together with 'save.folder' to write the methylation calls into a file that later can be read by 'methRead'. Or you could set the 'save.db' argument to save the created methylRaw object into a flat file database, which could be load later with 'readMethylDB' function.
>
> For the second question you can safely ignore the warning. This is something that has soon has to be addressed by us.
>
>
> I hope this helps you.
>
> Best,
> Alex
>
>
> Sent from mobile.
>
> Lei, Haiyan (NIH/NCI) [C] <lei.h...@nih.gov> schrieb am Do., 27. Mai 2021, 03:54:
> Hi, Alex:
>
> Thanks for your help last time. It almost worked, but I still have two questions.
> 1)How can I save the object and reuse next time? Such as I have the following object, and I want to save and use it next time, what can I do?
> objs=processBismarkAln(location=file.list,sample.id=list("10_MDB1425","3_MDB1447"),assembly="hg19",save.folder=NULL,save.context=NULL,read.context="CpG",nolap=FALSE,mincov=10,minqual=20,phred64=FALSE,treatment=c(1,0))
>
> 2) > cpg.obj=readFeatureFlank("cpgi.hg19.bed")
> Warning message:
> 'GenomicRangesList' is deprecated.
> Use 'GRangesList(..., compress=FALSE)' instead.
> See help("Deprecated")
>
> I have the wrong message for the above command, and not figure out how to fix it, can you give me some suggestions? Thanks very much.
>
> Best
>
> Haiyan
> From: Alexander Blume <alex....@gmail.com>
> Sent: Tuesday, May 25, 2021 12:08 PM
> To: Lei, Haiyan (NIH/NCI) [C] <lei.h...@nih.gov>
> Cc: Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com>
> Subject: Re: question about methylkit input files
>
> Hi Haiyan,
>
>
> Thank you for using methylKit for your research.
> It seems like you are specifying the path to your file in a wrong way.
>
> In your first call you are splitting the directory and the filename of your bam file, hence you are giving the first positional argument ( ‘location’ ) a directory path where it is expecting a file name pointing to a sam/bam file.
>
> obj=processBismarkAln("/gpfs/gsfs11/users/leihaiyan/Illumina_machinedata/SundayTaylor/Taylor_methyseq_042321/bismark_aligned.bam/sorted_ddbam","10_MDB1425_sorted.bam",assembly="hg19",save.folder=NULL,save.context="CpG",read.context="CpG")
>
> This is why the function fails with the error “fail to open sam/bam file”.
>
> In your second trial you are miss-using the system.file function, which is only meant to access internal data of the given package. You could inspect the content of ‘my.file’ which should be empty, hence you are error that your given location does not exist.
>
> As a small hint: Whenever you want to verify that you are giving a correct path, you could use the R function ‘file.exists()’.
>
>
> Best,
> Alex
>
>
>
> Alexander Blume
>
> PhD Student
> Berlin Institute for
> Medical Systems Biology (BIMSB)
> at Max Delbrueck Center (MDC)
> Hannoversche Str. 28
> 10115 Berlin, Germany
> Phone: +49 30 9406 1422
>
> Email: alexand...@mdc-berlin.de
> Web: https://www.mdc-berlin.de/bioinformatics
>
>
>
>
>
> On 25. May 2021, at 17:35, Lei, Haiyan (NIH/NCI) [C] <lei.h...@nih.gov> wrote:
>
> Dear Altuna and Alex:
>
> I want to use the methylkit, but I have some problems for the input files. I have the bismark align, bismark remove duplicate and samtools sorted bam files, but when I use the following command and got the wrong message,
>
> obj=processBismarkAln("/gpfs/gsfs11/users/leihaiyan/Illumina_machinedata/SundayTaylor/Taylor_methyseq_042321/bismark_aligned.bam/sorted_ddbam","10_MDB1425_sorted.bam",assembly="hg19",save.folder=NULL,save.context="CpG",read.context="CpG")
>
> [E::hts_hopen] Failed to open file /gpfs/gsfs11/users/leihaiyan/Illumina_machinedata/SundayTaylor/Taylor_methyseq_042321/bismark_aligned.bam/sorted_ddbam
> [E::hts_open_format] Failed to open file /gpfs/gsfs11/users/leihaiyan/Illumina_machinedata/SundayTaylor/Taylor_methyseq_042321/bismark_aligned.bam/sorted_ddbam
> Error in methCall(read1 = location, type = "bam", nolap = nolap, minqual = minqual, :
> fail to open sam/bam file: /gpfs/gsfs11/users/leihaiyan/Illumina_machinedata/SundayTaylor/Taylor_methyseq_042321/bismark_aligned.bam/sorted_ddbam
>
>
> I also tried this,
> > my.file=system.file("/gpfs/gsfs11/users/leihaiyan/Illumina_machinedata/SundayTaylor/Taylor_methyseq_042321/bismark_aligned.bam/sorted_ddbam", "10_MDB1425_sorted.bam", package = "methylKit")
> > obj=processBismarkAln(my.file,"10_MDB1425_sorted.bam",assembly="hg19",save.folder=NULL,save.context="CpG",read.context="CpG")
> Error in processBismarkAln(my.file, "10_MDB1425_sorted.bam", assembly = "hg19", :
> File supplied as the 'location' argument doesn't exist
>
> Can you please give me some suggestions? Or My bam files are not right? Thanks very much for your great suggestions.
>
> Best
>
> Haiyan
>
> <myDiff25p.csv>
